subject.title: Add accessibility config option to disable emojis and unicode symbols in TUI

question: Should OpenClaw add a durable core TUI plain-text accessibility setting, and what public config key, default, and ASCII replacement semantics should it use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but a new config surface and user-visible glyph replacement behavior become compatibility and accessibility product contracts.

options.title: Add Bounded TUI Plain-Text Mode
options.body: Implement an opt-in core TUI setting with ASCII replacements across tool cards, selectors, config metadata, docs, and tests while keeping rich glyphs as the default.

options.title: Defer Until Semantics Are Chosen
options.body: Keep the issue open but pause implementation until maintainers choose the public key, default, and replacement strings.

options.title: Reject Core Config For Now
options.body: Close only if maintainers explicitly decide glyph suppression should not be a core TUI capability despite the screen-reader reports.

recommendation.title: Add Bounded TUI Plain-Text Mode
recommendation.body: Implement an opt-in core TUI setting with ASCII replacements across tool cards, selectors, config metadata, docs, and tests while keeping rich glyphs as the default.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest routing signal is original and recent ownership across the TUI, tool-display, and config surfaces.
